Hi Sophie / Raj —

Quick recap from our call today and suggested next steps: 

- Use case: FinOpsCo wants to embed cost-optimized embeddings & generation into their billing UI; pilot scope = 2M tokens/month, 3-month pilot.
- Timing: target pilot start: early June.
- Procurement: we discussed AP path (PO vs card) and marketplace options — wanted to confirm your procurement readiness and preferred commercial path.

Attachments: Redwood_PRICING_Enterprise_20270501.xlsx (pricing), FinOpsCo_SOW_v1.pdf (draft SOW).

1) Marketplace purchase (if you prefer to avoid vendor onboarding) — typically fastest for legal/vendor-less procurement.
2) Standard PO/invoice (we accept PO and issue invoice Net30).
3) Card for initial pilot under $5k to accelerate kickoff while PO is processed.

Can you confirm: 1) which path is preferred, 2) procurement contact (name + email), and 3) any vendor onboarding docs we should pre-fill?

Thanks for the clear recap, Marissa — this is helpful. A few notes from procurement side: 

- FinOpsCo AP policy: any vendor expected to exceed $10k/month requires a formal PO and vendor onboarding (W-9, vendor setup form, tax info).
- Timeline: vendor onboarding + PO approval usually takes ~2-3 weeks once we have the W-9 and vendor packet completed.
- Marketplace: if Redwood is available via our preferred marketplace (CloudMarketplaceX) that is often faster as it bypasses our vendor onboarding; can you confirm if Redwood is listed?

For the pilot, our preference would be to avoid manual card management. If the pilot can stay under $5k and you can accept card only for the pilot, we could do that, but long-term procurement will require PO/invoice. 

Procurement contact: Raj Patel (raj.patel@finopsco.com) — looping him for next steps.

Thanks,
Sophie Li
Head of Product Operations | FinOpsCo
